sources.title: RFC 1337: TIME-WAIT Assassination Hazards in TCP

claims.text: RFC 9293 defines CLOSE-WAIT as waiting for the local user's termination request after the remote side has requested connection termination; receiving FIN in ESTABLISHED causes the TCP to signal the user, acknowledge the FIN and enter CLOSE-WAIT, while TCP half-close semantics allow the still-open direction to continue sending until the local application closes it.

RFC 9293 requires an actively closed connection to linger in TIME-WAIT for 2 x MSL; when a retransmitted FIN is received in TIME-WAIT the TCP acknowledges it and restarts the 2MSL timeout, preserving closure reliability when the final ACK was not received by the peer.

RFC 9293 describes TIME-WAIT as preventing delayed segments from a previous connection incarnation from being accepted by a later connection, and RFC 1337 analyzes hazards in which prematurely terminating TIME-WAIT can expose a new incarnation to old duplicate segments and corrupt connection behavior.

RFC 9293 defines close behavior by protocol state rather than client/server labels, documents simultaneous close progressing through CLOSING to TIME-WAIT, and permits reopening from TIME-WAIT only under stated sequence-number safeguards while pointing to timestamp-based improvements for high connection establishment rates.

findings: Primary RFC 9293 evidence supports the candidate's CLOSE-WAIT transition, half-close boundary, active-close TIME-WAIT requirement, retransmitted-FIN handling, simultaneous-close path and guarded TIME-WAIT reuse statements.

RFC 9293 together with RFC 1337 supports the two distinct 2MSL purposes explained by the candidate: closure reliability and isolation from old duplicate segments; the answer avoids presenting any operating-system-specific TIME_WAIT duration as a protocol constant.

Both assigned source-question variants are directly covered: the TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT comparison and the reason for waiting 2MSL. Diagnostic guidance is framed as investigation strategy rather than fabricated incident evidence or a universal sysctl prescription.

The concept answer has shared comparison dimensions, applicability and counterexample boundaries, topic-specific follow-ups, and a speakable short path; no blocker, critical, major or actionable minor finding remains for this candidate.
